spec.title: Cattaneo, Ma, Masatlioglu and Suleymanov, "A Random Attention Model" (Journal of Political Economy 128(7), 2020): simulation
spec.paper: Matias D. Cattaneo, Xinwei Ma, Yusufcan Masatlioglu and Elchin Suleymanov, A Random Attention Model, Journal of Political Economy 128(7): 2796-2836, 2020, doi 10.1086/706861
spec.cost_basis: GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04 runner, free for public repositories

setup.cmd: Rscript -e "u <- 'https://cloud.r-project.org/src/contrib/Archive/ramchoice/'; x <- readLines(u); m <- regmatches(x, regexec('(ramchoice_[0-9.-]+[.]tar[.]gz).*?([0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2})', x)); m <- do.call(rbind, Filter(function(v) length(v) == 3, m)); m <- m[as.Date(m[, 3]) > as.Date('2021-10-20'), , drop = FALSE]; f <- if (nrow(m)) m[order(as.Date(m[, 3])), 2][1] else NA; cat('installing', f, '\n'); install.packages('ramchoice', repos = 'https://cloud.r-project.org'); if (!is.na(f)) install.packages(paste0(u, f), repos = NULL, type = 'source'); stopifnot(requireNamespace('ramchoice'))"

scope_notes: The package is one R script, the simulation of the empirical size and power of the proposed revealed-preference test (1,000 repetitions, seed 42). It writes no file; it prints five rejection rates.
The script's own comments give the expected result (0.000, 0.004, 0.144, 0.275, 0.351). The printed rates are compared with those by hand, as set out in the protocol; the comparison is under notes.

`ramchoice` is the release current on 2021-10-20 (the script's date): the archived file with the earliest archive date after that day, chosen by the setup step; the version is in the environment listing.
